best_for: Students and engineers who learned MATLAB and need a free way to run their .m scripts on Windows or Linux, without a license server.
description:
GNU Octave is a free programming language for math and science, made under the GNU name. Its website copyright, dating back to 1998, is held by John W. Eaton. It is built for work with numbers, vectors and matrices.

You can solve a system of linear equations in one line with the backslash operator, or draw a 2D or 3D plot with a few short commands. The Octave wiki has more examples to copy and change. Octave has been a mentoring group in Google Summer of Code, and anyone can get the latest development source with Mercurial. If you want to support the work, the project takes donations on its site.

points.title: Runs most MATLAB code
points.text: Octave's language is built to be largely compatible with MATLAB, so many scripts run with little or no change. Expect to fix the odd function or toolbox call.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: Octave is free software under the GNU GPL. There is no paid edition and no account.

points.title: GUI, console or script
points.text: You can work in the graphical interface, in a terminal, or run Octave from a shell script for batch jobs. Extra functions come as packages listed at packages.octave.org.

points.title: A big Windows download
points.text: The Windows installer is about 540 MB, and the 7z and zip archives are about 460 MB and 820 MB. Builds are 64-bit only. The installer here can install for your user or for everyone on the PC.

points.title: No Mac build here
points.text: Octave's site has no official Mac installer; it points to its wiki and to Homebrew or MacPorts. This page lists Windows and Linux only.

points.title: Linux: verified Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build is marked verified for octave.org, for x64 and Arm64. Distribution packages also exist, kept by volunteers, so how current they are depends on your distribution.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 20 versions. Linux lists only the current Flatpak, so an older Linux build needs another source.
